The ADA didn't just change buildings and sidewalks. It changed expectations.

Our state remains fully committed to safeguarding the essential services and resources that empower individuals with disabilities to live independently. The progress made over the past 36 years will stay protected, no matter what changes come from the federal level.

The ADA was not an endpoint – but just the beginning of an initiative to leave no one behind.

No one should have to choose between protecting their health and keeping the power on.

As our state faces dangerous heat and unhealthy air quality due to the Canadian wildfires, the Maryland Public Service Commission has issued an emergency order halting electric service disconnections through July 24.

Check in on your neighbors, older adults, and anyone who may need extra support. We'll continue working together to do everything we can to keep Marylanders safe.
